sources.label: Metronome Synth deposit and mintage caps

reserveReview.rationale: Accessed 2026-09-30: the issuer supported-assets table names Ethereum DAI, USDC, FRAX, ETH, WBTC, sfrxETH and Vesper receipts, and Optimism/Base USDC and ETH-family collateral. These are eligible assets, not positive measured msUSD holdings. The July 30 post-mortem still describes approximately 4.57 million msUSD unbacked float and a remediation strategy involving looped treasury positions, LPs and buyback/burn; those July amounts do not establish current backing or a recovery guarantee. The public disclosure supplies no msUSD-only allocation rule for shared multi-synth collateral and no reconciled current debt/float/treasury statement. NC-136 remains basket-needs-split. Next evidence: obtain the issuer's synth-specific loss/claim allocation rule and reconciled dated debt, circulating float, and net treasury backing; then independently measure exact DepositToken and held-receipt claims at the same chain checkpoints. No eligible token is promoted to an edge.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Historical eligible collateral envelope; supported-assets and July 30 underbacking post-mortem re-read 2026-09-30, without a new measured composition
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Current deposited balances and weights across the eligible collateral set are not published in the reviewed issuer documentation, cross-margin multi-synth pooling prevents treating raw DepositToken supplies as msUSD-only composition, and the July 2026 post-mortem confirms a period of underbacking in the synth swap module that left approximately 4.57 million msUSD without matching debt positions.

providers.name: Metronome Synth per-asset DepositToken and Pool contracts (Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Hemi)
Vesper pool contracts underlying va-token collateral

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-2 (lead buidl-blackrock)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Collateral is pooled per asset in non-custodial DepositToken contracts with per-user debt tracked separately; plain assets (ETH, WBTC, USDC, DAI, FRAX) sit idle in those contracts, while Vesper va-token collateral (vaETH, vaUSDC, vaFRAX, and similar) represents positions whose underlying Vesper pools deploy capital into yield strategies by design, hence conditional reuse. The 2026-10-01 protocol and deployment-documentation review establishes technical per-asset contract separation, but did not establish enforceable legal segregation or bankruptcy-remoteness rights under ruling D09. Legal rehypothecation terms and a primary-source custody agreement were not located in that review.
